work.name: OmniVision Technologies, Inc.
work.summary: Develop algorithms in the ISP pipeline to improve image quality; standardize objective IQ metrics and A/B evaluations across sensors and releases.
highlights: Built a highlight-reconstruction module for saturated RAW regions (e.g., sky/LED), improving color accuracy (DeltaE00 ~10% vs baseline on over-exposed scenes) and restoring details.
Reduced denoise runtime by ~40% with a wavelet-based approach while maintaining SNR/texture on internal test sets.
Created an IQ toolkit (sharpness/MTF, SNR, visual noise) and standardized bring-up and A/B protocols.
Led image-quality validation and reporting for new ISP features and sensors from prototype to release.

work.name: Darkblue Technology, Inc.
work.summary: Developed computer-vision and control components for an agricultural robot; built an integrated Gazebo simulation to accelerate iteration.
highlights: Built the robot kinematic model using the D-H method and integrated it with control and perception.
Replaced RRT with BIT* for motion planning, producing shorter paths with fewer nodes in field-like simulations.
Implemented software camera sync (~0.1 s latency between two cameras) and deployed a detector reaching ~98% accuracy at ~10 FPS on an edge camera.
Integrated model, control, data transfer, and CV into a simulation of vision-servo behavior, reducing on-field iteration time by ~80%.

work.name: Midea Group
work.summary: Implemented a geometry-based pose estimator running in real time; generated synthetic data and built fast visualization tools.
highlights: Created a virtual camera system to simulate object-image projection mapping.
Projected RGB pixels from a target image onto the target’s 3D point cloud to stitch textures.
Generated simulated training data using OpenCV and Open3D to accelerate model development.
Built a portable Qt-based visualizer capable of ~100 FPS on commodity hardware.

awards.title: Merit Winner (top 8%) of Interdisciplinary Contest in Modeling (ICM)
